situation: A new Instagram customer sends only 'Price?' under a photo.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Price?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hello, thank you for your interest in Noolika! This saree is ₹2,400, including shipping.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Colours?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: It's available in red, green and navy. Shall I send photos of each?

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Send green.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Sure! Here are two photos in natural light. The colour may look slightly different on your screen.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Okay, nice.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Would you like me to reserve it for you until tomorrow?

keyExpressions: Would you like me to reserve it?
remember: Answer fast, then ask one question to keep the chat going.
Short customers need short replies. Don't send a long paragraph to 'Price?'

situation: A customer is ready to buy.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: I want the green one.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Lovely choice! It's in stock. Here are the payment details. Please send a screenshot after paying.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Paid. Sent screenshot.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I've received your payment. Thank you! Your order is confirmed. Could you please share your full address and PIN code?

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Sending now.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Thank you. Your order will be dispatched within two days. I'll send the tracking number as soon as it ships.

remember: Order of messages: stock, payment, confirmation, address, dispatch time.
Always promise the tracking number. It reduces 'where is my parcel?' messages.

situation: A customer asked about a saree two days ago and went silent.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hello Priya, just checking in - did you get a chance to look at the blue saree?

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Yes, but it's a bit costly for me.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I understand. This is our best price, as it's handwoven. I can offer ₹100 off on orders above ₹3,000, if you'd like to add another piece.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Let me think.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: No pressure at all - take your time. I'll keep it reserved until tomorrow evening.

remember: Give the reason for the price. Customers accept a reason more than a bare 'no'.
Follow up only once or twice.

situation: A customer is upset because the parcel is five days late.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: My saree hasn't come yet! It's been ten days.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I'm so sorry for the delay, and I understand how frustrating this must be. Could you share your order number?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Thank you. I've contacted the courier and will update you by 6 PM today.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Please do. I need it for a function.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Understood. If it can't reach you by Friday, we'll arrange a refund or a replacement - whichever you prefer.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Update: the courier says it's out for delivery tomorrow. Thank you for your patience.

keyExpressions: I'm so sorry for the delay.
I understand how frustrating this must be.
remember: Order: apology, feeling, action, time, choice.
Keep the time you promised. A late update is worse than none.

term: Saying No to a Return Politely
situation: A customer wants to return a customised blouse because she changed her mind.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: I want to return the blouse. I don't like the colour now.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Thank you for telling me. Unfortunately, we don't accept returns on customised items, because they're made just for you.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: That's not fair.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I understand your disappointment. What I can do is adjust the fit for free if it doesn't sit well.

conversation.speaker: Customer
conversation.text: Okay, let me check the fit.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Of course. Please send photos and I'll help.

remember: No + reason + what you CAN do. This is the polite way to refuse.
Stay calm. Don't repeat the policy more than once.
